correctness.rationale: The initiating full text proves that for general P the curve x↦O_C((g-1)x) meets the generalized theta divisor properly. The determinant character of rho is trivial from the hypotheses, so E_rho(P) has rank r and degree zero. Generalized theta theory gives divisor class r Theta. After identifying Pic^{g-1}(C) with J(C), the map is [g-1]∘j. The principal polarization satisfies [g-1]^*Theta ≡ (g-1)^2 Theta and Poincare's formula gives Theta·j(C)=g. Hence the pullback divisor has degree r g (g-1)^2. Riemann--Roch gives chi=0, so the H0- and H1-failure loci agree.

value.rationale: The exceptional locus controls precisely where the cohomological vanishing used in the new Hecke-curve stability argument fails. Its exact degree is a natural enumerative invariant of that setup and shows the finite failure locus is necessarily nonempty. The formula is uniform in both genus and representation rank and gives substantially more information than qualitative finiteness.
